title: Public /kpis: trend charts and a shared chart helper
description:
Repository: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour). One PR. Its sibling tickets: LIN-3711 (workspace page) reuses the helper this ticket builds; a small cost-figure ticket follows it in the same files.

## Why

The public KPIs page has four charts and no sparklines, and none shows how a figure moves day to day. John, 20 Oct: "There's maby a bit too much text, and some of the cumulative charts might be better as rates rather than totals (or we can toggle between)."

This ticket builds the charts the data already supports, as rates with short text. Running totals need a daily rollup; they and the rate/total toggle come with the separate rollup tickets (a design note, then a build). The chart code goes into one shared module, `public/chart-helpers.js`, so the workspace page can reuse it.

## What is true now

* The page draws four charts from `window.__KPI_DATA__` in `public/kpis.js`: `outcome-trend` bar (:82-113), `proxy-phases` stacked bar (:124-139), `dispatch-kinds`, `milestone-funnel`. `draw(name, amount, note, build)` is :50-61. No sparkline exists. Chart.js is vendored at `public/chart.umd.min.js`.
* `lib/render-kpis.js`: `statCard` :56-66, `headline` :74-90, `chartBox(name, title, {caption, anchor, rowsHtml})` :92-106 (canvas `chart-NAME`), hidden-count wording `HIDDEN_TEXT` :43-46, scripts :192. Canvas height rule: `public/kpis.css:142-151`.
* `buildDispatchOutcomes` (`lib/kpi-stats.js:688-727`) loops over lineages with each one's `status` (done/failed/aborted) and `earliest`, and keeps only `weeklyDone` and `weeklyResolved` (:691-692, :705-708). Weeks are 4 rolling 7-day buckets keyed on the lineage START, not its finish. Status and `statusMs` come from `groupDispatchLineages` (`lib/dispatch-lineage.js:158`, set at :236-239); `statusMs` can be null (:180).
* Per-day dispatch counts exist only as `dispatchByDay` (`kpi-stats.js:639-650`, :965): top-5 kinds plus `other`, not in the public view. `countByDay` (:153) is private. Autopilot runs are windowed rows with `kind === 'autopilot'` (`summarizeActivity`, :869).
* `toPublicKpis` (:1130-1157) emits `outcomes`, `totals`, `phases` (30 daily points per phase, axis `phases.days`), `dispatchKinds`, `milestoneFunnel`. `PUBLIC_LEAF_REGISTRY` (:1043-1056) must list every numeric leaf; a test fails on an unclassified one. Existing `open` leaves include `outcomes.weeklyResolved[]` and `phases.*[]`. The floor `PUBLIC_COUNT_FLOOR = 5` (:1026) covers "a count of people, or of per-person events" (:1023).
* The view's key list is pinned in `tests/unit/kpi-public-floor.test.js:239`, `tests/unit/render-kpis.test.js:59` and `tests/e2e/kpis.spec.js:80`; the chart-box count (4) at `kpis.spec.js:96`.

## Design

**Data (no new reads; every figure comes from rows** `collectKpiStats` **already loads).**

* `outcomes.weeklyFailed[]` and `outcomes.weeklyAborted[]`, beside `weeklyDone` in the loop. Per week, done = `weeklyResolved - failed - aborted`; no `weeklyDone` leaf.
* New top-level `daily`: `daily.dispatches[]`, `daily.autopilotRuns[]` (30 points each, `countByDay` over `windowedDispatchDocs`; export or reuse it) and `daily.done[]` (lineages with status `done`, counted on the day of `statusMs`, `skipped` excluded). A `done` lineage with null `statusMs` is not counted; the disclosure says so. `daily` has no `days` of its own: charts use `phases.days`, and a test asserts every `daily` array has `phases.days.length` points.
* Classification: register all five paths in `PUBLIC_LEAF_REGISTRY`. Class `open`, `why`: "run or lineage counts across every workspace; not tied to a person (same class as `outcomes.weeklyResolved[]`). A nonzero `phases` day already shows a run happened that day, so flooring these would hide nothing the page does not already show."
* `PUBLIC_COUNT_FLOOR` stays 5. Leave its comment, the test title and design doc :58 as they are.

**Charts** (title plus at most one plain "what it shows" line each; derivation goes in the disclosure):

* A1 sparklines on the existing cards, 30 daily points each: prompts dispatched (`daily.dispatches`), autopilot runs (`daily.autopilotRuns`), agent actions (sum of the five `phases` per day; label it "proxy calls per day", because the card total also counts agent-status reports, `kpi-stats.js:867`). None on the landed-rate headline or workspaces. No new tiles.
* A2 `outcome-weekly`: stacked done / failed / aborted bars per week. The caption must say "by start week".
* A3 `done-daily`: tasks finished per day, last 30 days, bars from `daily.done`. Rate only. The disclosure notes it counts on the day the agent marked `[done]` (not a verified merge) and differs from the headline, which counts by start.
* A4: `outcome-trend` becomes a line (weekly landed rate; null weeks are gaps). Keep the `n =` tooltip and the `#kpi-outcome-evidence` anchor.
* A5: `proxy-phases` keeps its stacked bars and gains a 7-day average line of total proxy calls. The line has 23 non-null points (none for the first 6 days or for today, which is partial). Title it "proxy calls". No phase-mix bar.

**Disclosure.** Every new or changed chart box gets `<details data-testid="kpis-numbers-NAME"><summary>Show the numbers</summary>` holding the derivation notes (server-rendered text) and the data table (built by the helper). Closed by default. Hidden-leaf wording comes from `HIDDEN_TEXT` via a data attribute on `<main>`, never a second copy in JS. The last row of any daily table is marked "today, so far".

**Shared helper.** New classic script `public/chart-helpers.js` (no build step), loaded before `/kpis.js`, exposing one global `HarbourCharts` with exactly three functions: `draw` (same behaviour as today; the colour tokens and Chart.js defaults move in from `kpis.js:19-36`), `sparkline(el, values, {label})` (inline SVG, colours from tokens, non-numbers break the line, `role="img"` with an aria-label) and `numbersTable(mount, {columns, rows, hiddenText})`. No rate/total toggle: the rollup build ticket adds it when it has a real total. Pure parts (the 7-day mean, sparkline point maths, table rows) are plain functions apart from the DOM code, so they test without a DOM; how the test reaches them is the worker's call. Nothing in the file may mention `kpi`, `__KPI_DATA__` or a page route. `kpis.js` keeps only page wiring. Do not touch the workspace page.

## Done when

1. `toPublicKpis` emits the five new leaves, each in `PUBLIC_LEAF_REGISTRY` as `open` with the `why` above; the registry walk passes. Per week, `weeklyFailed + weeklyAborted + done = weeklyResolved`. `sum(daily.dispatches) = totals.dispatches` and `sum(daily.autopilotRuns) = totals.autopilotRuns`.
2. Sparklines (30 points) show on the three cards named in A1, none on workspaces or the landed-rate headline.
3. `outcome-weekly`, `done-daily`, the A4 line and the A5 line draw from a seeded payload; an empty chart shows its note, as today.
4. Each chart box has a title, at most one visible line of text, and a closed "Show the numbers" disclosure holding the derivation note and a correct table. Hidden leaves read "fewer than 5" or "not shown" there.
5. No running total and no rate/total toggle is visible on the page.
6. No horizontal scroll at 390px with every disclosure open (tables sit in an `overflow-x: auto` wrapper).
7. The helper loads before `kpis.js`, exposes only `draw`, `sparkline`, `numbersTable`, and has no page-specific strings.
8. Existing look kept: page shell, fonts, colour tokens, vendored Chart.js. No new library.
9. `tests/unit/kpi-stats-reads-pin.test.js` passes unedited. If a read is added after all, update its snapshot and say why in the PR.

## Tests

* `tests/unit/kpi-stats.test.js`: failing-then-passing cases for `weeklyFailed`/`weeklyAborted` (start week, sum rule), `daily.done` (day of `statusMs`, `skipped` excluded, abort rows dropped, null `statusMs` not counted) and the dispatch and autopilot day sums.
* `tests/unit/kpi-public-floor.test.js`: the registry walk covers the new paths; update the key-list pin (:239). The title at :36 stays.
* `tests/helpers/public-kpis-fixture.js`: extend `buildStats` with the new fields and an option for a full 30-day series (the fixture has 2 phase days, :55-58).
* `tests/unit/render-kpis.test.js` and `tests/unit/chart-helpers.test.js` (new). Render: key list (:59); new test ids and disclosures; one visible line per chart box outside `<details>`; `chart-helpers.js` before `kpis.js`. Helpers: load the file in `node:vm` as `tests/unit/chat-append-options.test.js` does for chat.js; pin the 7-day mean (first 6 null), sparkline points (gaps, flat, single point, all null), table rows with hidden leaves, the three exported names, and no `kpi`/`__KPI_DATA__` in the source.
* `tests/e2e/kpis.spec.js`: update the key list (:80) and box count (:96). Add a seeded-payload spec: build a 30-day payload from `renderKpisPage`, `toPublicKpis` and the fixture, and `page.route('**/kpis')` to serve it. Assert each canvas has a live chart (`Chart.getChart(canvas)`), each sparkline has 30 points, the 7-day line has 23 non-null points, and each disclosure opens to the right row count. At 390x844 with all disclosures open, assert `scrollWidth - clientWidth <= 0` (extends :119-131).
* `tests/helpers.js` (:111-118): add `spark(name)` and `numbers(name)` to `SELECTORS.publicKpis`.

## Docs

* `public/llms.txt`: no change (`/kpis` stays unlinked). List the new test ids in `docs/plans/kpis-public-design.md` instead.
* `docs/plans/kpis-public-design.md`: new leaves in the registry table (:62-70); new charts in the chart table (:32-38). Leave :58 alone.
* `docs/architecture/source-map.md`: add `chart-helpers.js` beside `kpis.css / kpis.js` (:260); update the `render-kpis.js` (:108) and `kpi-stats.js` (:110) entries.
* CLAUDE.md: add nothing (at its line cap).

## Out of scope

The workspace KPI page and any reuse of the helper there; running totals, the rate/total toggle and the daily rollup; a landed-rate sparkline; a phase-mix bar; public cost, dropped on purpose (`docs/plans/kpis-public-design.md:25`); new tiles; changes to what the page reads or to the floor.

## Operator notes

**Rules for this run**

* No live calls to outside services (GitHub, Linear, OpenRouter, [harbour.cat](<http://harbour.cat>) or any other live host). Tests use the existing fakes.
* No paid model or OpenRouter calls.
* This is one PR. Don't split it into child tickets.
* No parallel forks or background sub-agents; one part at a time.
* Targeted tests while iterating (`node --test tests/unit/<file>.test.js`). Full unit suite (`npm run test:unit`) once before opening the PR. Leave e2e to CI.
* A failing-then-passing test is the witness for any behaviour change.
* Keep every existing ticket reference and every reason comment beside the code it governs; drop one only if its code is gone, and list those in the PR.
* A new production file (anything outside `tests/` and `docs/`) gets a pattern in `scripts/code-shape/areas.json` for the area that owns it, in the same PR. First match wins there, so check the file lands in that area and not in "Other features": run `node scripts/code-shape/seams.mjs . <commit>` at the base commit and at your final commit, report the area-pair count both times, and give the reason for any new pair. If it cannot run in your checkout (exit 2, `acorn` missing), record it as not run.
* Prompt text (templates, meta-prompt, runner prompt) is size-frozen (`tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js`). If you add prompt text, remove bytes elsewhere or raise the ceiling with the reason recorded beside it (LIN-3633), and say which in the PR.
* Where a choice is still open, keep today's behaviour, write it up as an open question in the PR, and carry on. Never stop to wait for a person. A check that needs a live service or a person is recorded in the PR as not run (what, why, follow-up), not a reason to hold the close.

## Implementation Plan

Implemented as approved in [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2003](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2003>) (merged as `c1d5c700`; plan grounded at `8f39afd8`). The plan's decisions held: `daily` computed in `collectKpiStats`, lineages grouped once, three-function `HarbourCharts`, `trailingMean` reaching `kpis.js` via `build(canvas, tools)`, no `areas.json` edit. Deviation: the 390px witness was strengthened at close-out (`d75363bf`) after review found it could never fail under `overflow-x: clip`. The full plan text is preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

Session fit: fits one session.

comments.body: Plan added to the description under ## Implementation Plan. Single viable strategy, no routed-around gap (none identified). Session fit: one session, one PR, no subtasks. plan-review due: no (none of (a)-(d)). Open question carried to the PR: trailingMean reaches kpis.js via build(canvas, tools) so the helper keeps exactly three exports. Not run: no code changed at this stage; seams baseline at 8f39afd8 is 11 areas / 66 links.

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2003 (commit c87a4183). CI green: ci-success, unit, E2E shards 1-4, secret scan.

Built per the plan: five new `open` registry leaves (`outcomes.weeklyFailed/weeklyAborted`, `daily.dispatches/autopilotRuns/done`); `public/chart-helpers.js` (classic script, exactly `draw`/`sparkline`/`numbersTable`, no page strings); sparklines on three cards; `outcome-weekly`, `done-daily`, line `outcome-trend`, 7-day line on `proxy-phases` (23 non-null points); closed "Show the numbers" disclosures with server-rendered notes; hidden wording via `<main data-hidden-text>`. Workspace page untouched; floor and its wording unchanged.

Evidence: `npm run test:unit` 18793 pass / 0 fail (reads-pin test unedited); kpis.spec.js run locally 14/14 incl. seeded 30-day payload and 390px no-scroll with all disclosures open; kpi-stats tests failed first (daily/weeklyFailed undefined), render test mutation-checked. Seams at c87a4183: 11 areas / 66 links, same as baseline 8f39afd8.

Choices: `trailingMean` goes to kpis.js via `build(canvas, tools)` (exports stay three; a fourth export is a one-line change if preferred); empty-note class is passed via the canvas's `data-empty-class` since the helper may not contain "kpi". Left open: no visible count of done rows omitted for null `statusMs` (the disclosure states the rule).

## Review — LIN-3710

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2003 at head `c87a4183` (base `8f39afd8`, which is still `origin/main`). No commits have touched the ticket's files since it was created, so the plan is current. The diff stays within the plan's surfaces S1–S4. The workspace page, `PUBLIC_COUNT_FLOOR`, `areas.json`, `llms.txt` and CLAUDE.md are unchanged.

CI: green on c87a4183 (Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan, CI success). I re-ran the checks myself: `npm run test:unit` gives 18793 pass / 0 fail, and `tests/e2e/kpis.spec.js` passes 14/14 locally. Seams gives 11 areas / 66 links at both base and head, with an identical area import map.

### What I checked
- **Done-when 1–5 and 7–9**: each one is met in the code and by a test. The five leaves are registered `open` with the `why` from the description, and there is no `weeklyDone` leaf. `daily` is built in `collectKpiStats`, not in the shared `summarizeActivity`. Lineages are grouped once. `chart-helpers.js` exposes exactly three functions, is a classic script with no `kpi` string, and loads before `kpis.js`. `HIDDEN_TEXT` reaches the script only through `<main data-hidden-text>`. The `n =` tooltip and `#kpi-outcome-evidence` anchor are kept. The reads-pin test was not edited.
- **Mutation checks** (each mutation was reverted afterwards). All of these went red:
  - counting `daily.done` by `earliest` instead of `statusMs`
  - dropping the `weeklyFailed` increment
  - counting skipped lineages as done
  - removing the autopilot filter
  - making the sparkline skip gaps instead of breaking the line
  - making `trailingMean` return 0 during the first six days instead of null
  - removing `data-hidden-text`
  - swapping the script order
  - in e2e: not nulling today's 7-day point (the 23-point test fails)
  - in e2e: giving the sparkline 29 points instead of 30

  One mutation survived but is equivalent: removing the `statusMs === null` guard changes nothing, because `utcKey(null)` already returns null, so the day lookup misses.
- **The 390px test cannot fail (finding, inside done-when 6).** I removed `overflow-x: auto` from `.kpi-numbers-wrap` and the seeded "no horizontal scroll at 390px with every disclosure open" test stayed green. I measured why: the proxy-phases table is 734px wide. Without the wrapper rule it spills out to `body` (scrollWidth 778 against 375), but `html`/`body` have `overflow-x: clip` (`public/style.css:284,304`, LIN-1068). So `documentElement.scrollWidth - clientWidth` is always ≤ 0, and the content would just be cut off without any test noticing. The PR's own CSS is correct: as shipped, the wrapper scrolls (scrollWidth 734 inside 287px with overflow auto) and nothing leaks. Only the test is blind. This is the same trap LIN-2830 hit (`7700f6d8`), and `tests/e2e/session-decision-layout.spec.js:13` already documents the idiom as reading 0. The older test at `kpis.spec.js:122-133`, which this ticket extends, has the same hole.
- **Manual check**: I took screenshots of the seeded page at 1280px light and 390px dark with the proxy-phases disclosure open. The charts, sparklines, null-week gap and "today, so far" row all render. The table scrolls inside its own wrapper, and the shell and tokens are unchanged.
- **Nit, not required**: `public/kpis.js` `meanOf` repeats `trailingMean`'s rule so the table can show the 7-day average, which means there are two implementations that could drift apart. This is a side effect of keeping three exports (open question 1). The test that compares rows doesn't compare the values.
- **Open questions**: `trailingMean`, and also `ink`, reach the page through `build(canvas, tools)` instead of a fourth export. There is still no visible count of done lineages with a null `statusMs`. Both keep today's behaviour as the plan said, and neither blocks the merge.
- **One of a class?** The `documentElement.scrollWidth` check also appears in `tests/e2e/runner-setup.spec.js:185`. That is a different page and outside this ticket's classes. Close-out should file one ticket, after checking it doesn't already exist: "documentElement scrollWidth overflow checks are vacuous under the site-wide `overflow-x: clip`". Apart from that, the change has no unhandled siblings. The workspace page doesn't load this payload or this script.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Done-when 6, no horizontal scroll at 390px with disclosures open: inside** (done-when 6 / plan S3 "390px no-scroll check"). Settle before the merge. Close-out should replace the overflow assertion in both `tests/e2e/kpis.spec.js` tests, the seeded "no horizontal scroll at 390px with every disclosure open" and the older "renders without horizontal overflow on mobile", with a rendered-geometry assertion:
  - `document.body.scrollWidth <= document.body.clientWidth`
  - for every `[data-testid^="kpis-chart-"]` and `[data-testid^="kpis-card-"]`: `el.scrollWidth <= el.clientWidth`
  - in the seeded test, for every `.kpi-numbers-wrap`: computed `overflowX === 'auto'`

  The condition that tells right from wrong: delete `overflow-x: auto` from `.kpi-numbers-wrap` in `public/kpis.css` and the seeded test must go red (the proxy-phases box measures scrollWidth 750 against clientWidth 319). Restore the rule and it must pass.
- **Done-when 1 sum rules on live data: inside** (done-when 1 / plan risk "sum invariant is seeded-data only"). Settle after deploy, as a post-deploy step, not a merge condition. On live `/kpis`, read `window.__KPI_DATA__`:
  - `sum(daily.dispatches)` should equal `totals.dispatches`, and `sum(daily.autopilotRuns)` should equal `totals.autopilotRuns`. Any gap must be explained by rows dated after `generatedAt`.
  - For every week, `weeklyResolved - weeklyFailed - weeklyAborted >= 0`.
  - `sum(daily.done)` should be nonzero if `outcomes.done > 0`. A zero here would mean `statusMs` is missing on real done lineages.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger. The feature is complete and correct against done-when 1–9, and its unit and e2e witnesses held up under mutation. The one exception is the 390px no-scroll witness: under the site-wide `overflow-x: clip` it can never fail, so close-out must strengthen it as described above before merging.

## Close-out — LIN-3710

**Merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2003, squash-merged as `c1d5c700` with `--match-head-commit d75363bf`. Deployed: live `/kpis` footer shows `c1d5c700` and serves `chart-helpers.js` before `kpis.js`.

**Review verdict:** Approve, conditional on the ledger below.

### Change I made (answers the review's "What CI Did Not Prove", done-when 6)
- `d75363bf` (`tests/e2e/kpis.spec.js` only): both 390px tests ("renders without horizontal overflow on mobile" and the seeded "no horizontal scroll at 390px with every disclosure open") read `documentElement.scrollWidth - clientWidth`, which is always 0 under `overflow-x: clip`. They now call a shared `expectNoClippedOverflow` helper: `body.scrollWidth <= body.clientWidth`, every `kpis-chart-*` / `kpis-card-*` box `scrollWidth <= clientWidth`, and (seeded test) every `.kpi-numbers-wrap` computes `overflow-x: auto`. No production code changed, so no stale citation or comment came out of it.

### Ledger
1. **390px witness (inside, before merge): settled.** Mutation run by me: with `overflow-x: auto` deleted from `.kpi-numbers-wrap` in `public/kpis.css`, the seeded test fails (`body` overflow Received 403, Expected <= 0); with the rule restored, `kpis.spec.js` passes 14/14. The CSS was restored (`git checkout`) and is not part of the diff. The mutated run showed only the seeded test red; the older mobile test (which does not open the disclosures) stays green on the mutation, as expected, since it checks the closed page.
2. **Sum rules on live data (inside, post-deploy): settled on live `/kpis` at `c1d5c700`** (payload generated 2026-10-20T11:22Z):
   - `sum(daily.dispatches)` = 12806 = `totals.dispatches`; `sum(daily.autopilotRuns)` = 450 = `totals.autopilotRuns`.
   - Every `daily` array has 30 points, equal to `phases.days`.
   - Per week `weeklyResolved - weeklyFailed - weeklyAborted` = 829, 622, 777, 744 (all >= 0).
   - `sum(daily.done)` = 3013 and `outcomes.done` = 3057, so `statusMs` is present on real done lineages. The two differ by design: one counts by finish day within 30 days, the other by start.
3. **Outside: documentElement.scrollWidth checks vacuous under `overflow-x: clip`** filed as LIN-3715 (Medium, `Improvement` + `kind:follow-up` + `front:surfaces`), related to LIN-2491 and LIN-3710. Search found no existing ticket for it.
4. **No named monitor or rollback** was in the ledger.
5. **Nit (not required), `meanOf` in `kpis.js` repeating `trailingMean`'s rule:** left as is, the cost of keeping exactly three exports (open question 1). Not filed: inside this ticket's design, and the review marked it non-blocking.

### Open questions carried (current behaviour kept)
- `trailingMean` (and `ink`) reach the page through `build(canvas, tools)` rather than a fourth export; a fourth export is a one-line change if wanted.
- No visible count of done lineages with null `statusMs`; the disclosure states the rule.

### CI and checks
- CI exists and was green on the exact merged head `d75363bf`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, Secret scan (source), CI success (run 39412874923), read fresh before the merge.
- Review's own run on `c87a4183`: `npm run test:unit` 18793 pass / 0 fail; seams 11 areas / 66 links at base and head. I did not rerun the full unit suite locally on `d75363bf` (only a test file changed; CI ran it).
- Not run: none outstanding.

### Housekeeping
- Description archived (snapshot captured 2026-10-20T11:07Z, verified equal to the pre-prune text) and the Implementation Plan body pruned to a stub; the problem statement, design, done-when, tests, docs and operator notes are kept.
- Tickets tidied: LIN-3711 (workspace page, Todo) now has the shared helper to reuse; noted there. LIN-3712, LIN-3713, LIN-3714 and LIN-3709 are not settled by this work and are untouched.

issue.title: e2e overflow checks that read documentElement.scrollWidth are vacuous under the site-wide overflow-x: clip (tests/e2e/runner-setup.spec.js:185)
